question: The ratio of the ages of P and Q is 13 : 11. Note that 1 Decade = 10 years. The total of their ages is 3.6 decades. What is the proportion of their ages after 0.75 decades?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total parts of present ages = 13 + 11 = 24 parts.

Total age = 3.6 decades = 36 years ⇒ 1 part = 36 ÷ 24 = 1.5 years.

Present age: P = 13 × 1.5 = 19.5 years, Q = 11 × 1.5 = 16.5 years.

After 0.75 decades (7.5 years): P = 19.5 + 7.5 = 27 years, Q = 16.5 + 7.5 = 24 years.

Proportion after 7.5 years = 27 : 24 = 9 : 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of present ages of P and Q = 13 : 11

Total age of P and Q = 3.6 decades

1 Decade = 10 years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total present age = 3.6 × 10 = 36 years

⇒ Let the present ages of P and Q be 13x and 11x respectively.

⇒ 13x + 11x = 36

⇒ 24x = 36

⇒ x = 36 ÷ 24 = 1.5

⇒ Present age of P = 13 × 1.5 = 19.5 years

⇒ Present age of Q = 11 × 1.5 = 16.5 years

⇒ After 0.75 decades, time passed = 0.75 × 10 = 7.5 years

⇒ Age of P after 7.5 years = 19.5 + 7.5 = 27 years

⇒ Age of Q after 7.5 years = 16.5 + 7.5 = 24 years

⇒ Required proportion = 27 : 24

⇒ Simplest ratio = 9 : 8

**∴ The correct answer is 9 : 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Ages

If the current ages are in the ratio a : b, their ages after t years will be in the ratio (ax + t) : (bx + t), where x is the common multiplier.

Concept of Decades

A decade represents a period of 10 years. Therefore, to convert any value given in decades into years, simply multiply the value by 10.

Proportion

A proportion is an equation which states that two ratios are equal. It helps in establishing a relationship between multiple quantities sharing the same ratio base.
